monument_name: Vināyaka Pañcadevala Śikhara Temple 4 (built between the late 13th and early 14th cent.)
description_en: Vināyaka Pañcadevala Śikhara Temple 4, built between the late 13th and early 14th centuries, is situated on a large platform that houses four medievalśikharatemples and one more recent shrine. The complex is in Binayak (Vināyaka), one of the Achham district's main market towns.Temple 4 is one of the two large centralśikharasand is likely the best-preserved Temple at the Vināyaka Pañcadevala Śikhara Temple Complex. On both sides of the door,antarāla(skt.) projections frame the entrance to the sanctum. In front of each doorjamb, just before the threshold, a column is erected. The bases of the two columns are square and the shafts are square in the lower half and have multiple faces in the upper half. The lower halves are adorned with pyramidal motifs found on mediaeval stone memorial pillars. A cruciform capital crowns them. The sanctum houses a small stoneśivaliṅgadirectly set in the ground.The ceiling is a carved slab embellished with a finely carved rosette. The pediment differs slightly from that seen on the 'twin'śikharatemple to the southeast of ACH0072, as it contains a central flat surface separating moulded plinths.This Temple 4 was most likely built around the same time as its 'twin' to the southeast (ACH0072), i.e. in the late 13th or early 14th century. Indeed, the proportions of the two monuments are nearly identical, as they are lined up and oriented in the same direction.The monuments of Binayak are described by Prayag Sharma (Sharma 1972).Please see Vināyaka Pañcadevala Śikhara Mandira 1 (ACH0070), Mandira 2 (ACH0071) and Mandira 3 (ACH0072) for more information on the Pañcadevala plan implemented in west Nepal'sśikharatemples.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
